review_status: draft v1 - giant reef snapper profile

profile.diet: Spiny lobsters, large crabs, and reef fishes
profile.behavior: Largest Atlantic snapper; holds in deep reef ledges and wrecks, forming full-moon summer spawning aggregations.

factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, ideal for cubera snapper.
factors.value_notes: FishBase reports a model-derived preferred-temperature estimate of 21.7–27.6 °C (mean 25.5 °C) based on 100 cells. This overlaps the configured 22–30 °C range and 24–28 °C ideal, but it is a distribution model estimate, not a direct physiological experiment or local catch-response curve.

factors.reason_template: Structure is {value}, where giant cubera snapper hide.
factors.value_notes: Florida Museum and BOEM describe cubera snapper as reef-associated, using rocky ledges/overhangs, deep reefs, and wrecks. This supports the broad structure association but does not validate the exact category ranking or numeric map scores.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, in deep reef habitat.
factors.value_notes: Florida Museum reports depths to about 55 m; BOEM reports adults to about 85 m and spawning aggregations at 67–85 m. This supports reef-depth use but does not validate the configured 18–90 m range or 30–60 m ideal as a general preference. Depth is an active gate.

text.night: It is night, when nocturnal feeding is high.
text.dusk: It is dusk, a low-light time when fish feed actively.
text.dawn: It is dawn, a low-light time when fish feed actively.
